[@pruscinoEffectsCompressionGarments2013] | 8 competitive male hockey players (21.9±2.3 years; 1.80±0.08m; 77.9±13.9kg) | Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test with intensity relative to VO2max of each ppt | Compression garments worn for 48 hours after completion of exercise | No significant differences between conditions for IL-6, creatine kinase or muscle function (p >0.05). Perceived recovery was elevated in compression garment group (p =0.005). |  |
| Ferguson et al. * [@fergusonNeuromuscularElectricalStimulation2014] | 21 male team-sports players (21±1 year; 1.79±0.07m; 76±9kg) | Adapted Loughborough intermittent shuttle test: 2x45 min intermittent exercise relative to VO2max with 15 mins in between bouts | Graduated compression socks worn for at least 12 hours following exercise | No differences between conditions for biochemical markers. No time x treatment interaction for strength (p =0.71) | *Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation not reviewed in this study |
| French et al. * [@frenchEffectsContrastBathing2008] | 16 resistance trained males (22.7±2.3 years; 1.83±0.07m; 83.1±9.3kg) | 6x10 back squats with 100% body weight loaded with 5s eccentric negative phase at the end of each set | Compression tights worn for 12 hours (overnight) following exercise | No additive effect on recovery for performance, perceptual or biochemical variables at any time point | *Contrast trial can be found in heat and contrast table |
